On Wed, Mar 3, 2027 at 11:02 AM Evan Price <evan.price@borealis.ai> wrote:
> Naomi —
> 
> Appreciate the clear MAP. Quick responses from our side: ...

Thanks Evan — adding a suggested sequencing below that maps MSA/DPA/Order Form dependencies to onboarding gates. I attached a one-page sequence diagram in the MAP workbook but pasted the highlights here.

Sequencing (recommended):
- Step 1: Legal review (redline) — Borealis legal provides redline back to Redwood (target 5 business days from today).
- Step 2: Technical evidence provisioning — Redwood to deliver SOC2 Type II summary, pen test cover page, KMS integration note (2 business days after redline receipt).
- Step 3: Pricing & Order Form alignment — Redwood and Borealis finalize order form; Redwood sends final Order Form + invoice to procurement (3 business days after evidence delivered).
- Step 4: PO issuance & execution — Borealis issues PO; both sign MSA/OrderForm (10 business day approval window).
- Step 5: Provisioning & pilot acceptance — Redwood provisions pilot IDs, runs acceptance smoke tests; roll to pilot in two phases (canary 10% then full).

Acceptance gates (brief):
- Gate A: Security evidence satisfied (SOC2, pen test summary)
- Gate B: MSA/DPA agreed (no unresolved high-risk redlines)
- Gate C: Order Form + PO received

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Legal stalls on indemnity/PII clauses — Mitigation: offer limited term patch (pilot license) to shorten timeline.
- Risk: KMS integration scope creeps — Mitigation: offer hosted HSM option for pilot to avoid heavy infra changes.

Action owners:
- Naomi: coordinate commercial terms + scheduling
- Jordan: finalize Order Form template and pricing line items
- Kimberly: prepare onboarding checklist + test plan for acceptance
- Rishi: escalate any SLA exceptions and validate provisioning lead times with infra team

Attaching: updated MAP workbook (Borealis_MAP_v1.xlsx) with sequence tab and a short sequence diagram.

-Rishi

Team —

Quick procurement notes from our side: 

- PO lead times: our finance team requires a clean Order Form and an approved pricing sheet to start the PO. Typical routing is 7–10 business days.
- Security evidence: SOC2 Type II report (redacted) + pen test summary should be attached when you present to our InfoSec.
- Data residency: must be US-only (us-east-1). If Redwood can guarantee that for the pilot and the logs are retained per our retention policy, that will clear 70% of our InfoSec checklist.

Other items for clarity: 
- Billing: we prefer net-45 for pilots under $50k; anything above will go to an exec approval queue.
- KMS: our security team prefers customer-managed keys but can accept vendor-managed keys for a short pilot if we have an on-call runbook.

Next steps from Borealis: Liam will circulate a preliminary timeline for legal review (he indicated 4–6 business days to produce redlines). Procurement will start internal routing once we have the final Order Form (Jordan, happy to have you share the draft).

Thanks —
Maya
